top_concerns: Under‑ranking of acute cardiac syndrome / cardiorenal syndrome as primary problem
Therapeutic gaps (no ACE‑I/ARB, statin, antiplatelet, SGLT2‑i)
Low probability assigned to congestive hepatopathy despite supporting urine bilirubin
Inclusion of unsupported acute tubular injury diagnosis
recommended_primary: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with chronic heart failure (cardiorenal syndrome type 2)
review_summary: The junior differential captured the major chronic diseases but mis‑prioritized the acute, life‑threatening cardiac syndrome and included an unsupported tubular injury diagnosis. Adjusted probabilities reflect the dominance of cardiorenal syndrome and diabetic‑hypertensive nephropathy, elevate the relevance of congestive hepatopathy, and remove the unsupported entity. Management gaps are highlighted as a critical omission.
